Subject: Finova performance SLOs + regional routing / data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Sabrina
- great to chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary from call:
- Primary workloads: user-facing chat (low-latency generation), nightly batch embeddings for search, and a reranking pipeline for personalization.
- Expected Q2 traffic: peak 800 rps across the API, average 250 rps; concurrent active sessions estimated 120.
- Latency targets: p95 generation <= 300ms for US users, <= 350ms for EU users, <= 450ms APAC (initial). Streaming for long responses preferred (token-by-token).
- Throughput/concurrency: expect bursts up to 1200 rps during marketing pushes; single-request concurrency per user varies with streaming enabled.
- Data residency: EU user data must remain in EU regions; APAC routed to APAC region where possible.

Action items I committed to:
1) Share an SLO matrix with region-specific latency/throughput configurations (attached).
2) Connect Finova security with our compliance doc + SOC2 evidence request (attached).
3) Follow up with our infra lead on regional routing behavior and cross-region fallbacks (looping in Vivek).
4) Schedule a short tech deep-dive to confirm streaming protocol (gRPC vs HTTP streaming) and KV cache behavior.

Next steps / proposed meeting:
- Tech deep-dive: Thu Apr 1, 10:00 PT (30m)
- Vivek and Neha to join. Confirm if that works for Tom/Sabrina.

I attached a first-pass SLO matrix and a network topology checklist
- please review and flag anything missing.

Best,
Marissa

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa
- this is perfect. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: the p95 numbers look right. For critical checkout flows we need p99 <= 700ms in the US; can Redwood provide both p95 and p99 regionally?
2) Streaming: we prefer token streaming for customer-facing chat (so UX shows tokens as they arrive). gRPC streaming is fine, but we need to confirm browser fallback behavior for clients that cannot use gRPC (SSE or chunked HTTP).
3) Data residency: EU-attributed user content must never leave EU processing
- can you confirm Redwood can guarantee EU-only processing and storage for EU user requests? If you require fallback to US for capacity we'll need an explicit policy and prior approval.

Tom, can you add any infra constraints on our side?

Thanks
- Sabrina

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Finova performance SLOs + regional routing / data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Sabrina
- looping in answers to the technical points and adding a few questions for sizing: 

Regional SLOs & routing:
- We can provide p95 and p99 latency SLOs per-region (US, EU, APAC) and expose metrics in the console and via Prometheus endpoints.
- For EU data residency: we support EU-only processing + storage when using a dedicated region (Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC). Hosted mode can be configured with strict EU routing, but we do use cross-region fallback only when explicitly enabled in the routing policy. We will not fail-over EU-attributed requests to US without explicit approval.

Streaming & browser fallback:
- We support gRPC streaming and HTTP chunked streaming (server-sent events / SSE) for browser clients. We recommend SSE as the fallback for browsers that cannot use gRPC.

Throughput / concurrency assumptions (for capacity planning):
- Baseline model config used for estimation: 8k context, 16k kv cache, medium-throughput batch kernels.
- For p95 <= 300ms (US) with streaming enabled, we estimate required capacity: 10 dedicated GPU slots (A100-like throughput) to handle 800 rps with <=200ms per-token latency under continuous batching.
- Burst headroom to 1200 rps needs autoscaling + burst buffer; for Dedicated we can provision burst capacity and guarantee warm cache for your hottest prefixes.

Questions:
1) Can you share expected average tokens per request and distribution of short vs long responses? (we assumed avg 120 tokens per response; if many 1k+ responses we need to size differently)
2) Does Finova require content residency for embeddings indexes (search indices) as well as raw request/response logs?

I'll bring a short SLO-by-region proposal to the tech deep-dive.

- Vivek
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek
- quick answers from infra/security: 
- Avg tokens: for chat flows ~140 tokens avg, but ~15% of requests are long form (600-1200 tokens).
- Embeddings: search indices must be stored in EU when indexed from EU users; we can mirror non-sensitive indices to other regions for read-only caching but primary storage must be EU.
- We prefer not to enable cross-region fallback for EU unless there's an emergency; we will allow it with an exception process.

We will review the attached SOC2 request and send the initial security questionnaire (Finova internal) by EOD Wed.

Tom
Head of Infra, Finova
